column2: Population by economy GNI per capita relative to the world average, 2026

World Bank WDI, GNI per capita, Atlas method (NY.GNP.PCAP.CD) and population (SP.POP.TOTL); World Bank OGHIST (1 July 2026) for the operational thresholds; UN World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant; author's calculations and projections. Schellekens 2026, The Great Income Inversion, Moving Frontiers.
Bands are multiples of world GNI per capita, $14801 in 2026. Population is the sum over economies falling in each band.
5.20 billion people, 64 percent of the total, live in an economy below the world average.
China is nowcast to cross above the world average in 2026, at 1.01 times, which places its 1.4 billion people in the 1 to 2x band; on 2025 actuals China sat below the line.
Every person carries their own country's average, so these are measures of inequality between countries, not within them. A survey-based measure would be considerably wider.

Values from 2026 reflect a nowcast based on a conservative constant-pace scenario that replicates country-level median per capita income growth over the last decade. See Schellekens 2026 for methodology.
